title: The bent woman (Luke 13:10–17)
hook: eighteen years bent over, healed on the sabbath, and she stands straight

segments.voice: Yesterday, a gardener begged one more year for a fig tree with no figs. Your line was let it alone this year.

Try this for a moment. Let your head drop and your back curl until you're looking at the floor. Stay there. You can see feet, and dust, and the hems of other people's clothes. You can't see a face unless someone bends down to you. Now imagine that for eighteen years: going to the market like that, going to the synagogue like that. Luke says there was a woman who lived this way, and one sabbath Jesus was teaching in her synagogue.
screen: `LOOK AT THE FLOOR. STAY THERE.` → `EIGHTEEN YEARS OF FEET AND DUST.` → `ONE SABBATH IN THE SYNAGOGUE.`

segments.voice: Luke describes her carefully: "there was a woman, who had a spirit of infirmity eighteen years: and she was bent down, neither could she look upwards at all." She doesn't ask for anything. Luke only says she was there. Jesus sees her and calls her over: "Woman, thou art delivered from thy infirmity." He lays his hands on her, and immediately she's made straight, and she glorifies God. Then a complication. The ruler of the synagogue is indignant, because it's the sabbath. There are six days for work, he tells the crowd. Come and be healed on those. It's fair to see what he's protecting. Keeping the sabbath holy was, and is, a deep act of faithfulness for Jews. Jesus answers from inside that same faithfulness. Every one of you unties his ox or his donkey on the sabbath and leads it to water. And this woman, a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has bound these eighteen years, shouldn't she be untied on the sabbath day? Daughter of Abraham: the title gives her back her full place among God's people. In Jesus' reading, the sabbath is exactly the day for setting someone free. Luke ends with the crowd rejoicing at all the glorious things he was doing.
screen: `EIGHTEEN YEARS, BENT DOWN.` · `WOMAN, THOU ART DELIVERED.` · `THE OX UNTIED ON THE SABBATH.` · `A DAUGHTER OF ABRAHAM.` · then, large: `SHE WAS MADE STRAIGHT.`

segments.voice: If you're able, stand; if not, sit tall, and start bent, head dropped and shoulders curled, breathing there a moment. Then slowly unroll your spine until your head rises and you're looking straight ahead, and think of one thing you're grateful for today. If you pray, give thanks to God the way she did; if you don't, simply let yourself feel glad to be upright.
Infirmity. Eighteen years unable to look up, healed by Jesus on the sabbath and called a daughter of Abraham. Today's word.
Your line: she stood up. Eighteen years of looking at the floor, and then she looked up. That's day four hundred sixty-six.

fork.setup: you lead the synagogue. a teacher has just healed a woman on the sabbath, and the crowd is buzzing. what do you say?
options: there are six days for healing. come on those.
praise God, and invite him to teach again.

trapdoor: what you thought: this story is about Jesus breaking a rule.
what it means: Jesus argues from within sabbath faithfulness that the sabbath is the right day to set a daughter of Abraham free.
what a scholar hears: the verb for her being made straight (anorthoo) is the one the Greek Psalms use for God lifting up those bowed down (Psalm 145:8).

chat.says: Why was the synagogue leader upset that Jesus healed the woman?
options: He was protecting the sabbath; Jesus said it's the very day to free her.
He thought she was faking it and had never really been bent at all.
He was angry that Jesus had come to teach without being asked.
chat.meaning: The ruler said come on the six work days; Jesus answered that if an ox is untied on the sabbath, a daughter of Abraham should be too.

sabbath.meaning: the weekly day of rest, kept holy

synagogue.meaning: a Jewish house of prayer and teaching

daughter of Abraham.meaning: Jesus' title for her: her full place among God's people
